newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA CALL UP LOCAL YOUTH, DROP KOLYVANOV.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA CALL UP LOCAL YOUTH, DROP KOLYVANOV.

text.p: Russia head coach Boris Ignatyev has called up a quartet of debutants from the domestic league for next week's World Cup qualifier against Luxembourg and dropped three exiled stars, including Bologna's Igor Kolyvanov.

The striker, who failed to score in last month's 1-1 draw in Cyprus, and Celta Vigo midfielder Alexander Mostovoy, who missed a sitter in the dying minutes, appear to be paying the price for dropping two points against the group five outsiders.

Ignatyev said on Monday that the pair, along with Valencia midfielder Valery Karpin, were victims of a change of tactics -- precisely what change he would not say -- and denied he was bowing to popular discontent with foreign-based players.
Kolyvanov has been injured, Ignatyev noted, but his absence from the squad was a result of the change of strategy.

Ignatyev, who took over from Oleg Romantsev after a disastrous European championship campaign last year, has himself frequently voiced doubts about the commitment and patriotism of the "legionnaires" who have quit the domestic league for riches in the West.

His 23-man squad for the April 30 clash at Moscow's Dynamo Stadium includes first-time call-ups for in-form CSKA striker Vladimir Kulik and Alexander Gorshkov, a midfielder from this season's surprise early contenders Zhemchuzhina Sochi.
"These lads have performed well in the domestic championship and it's convenient for us because they're near at hand and we can keep our eye on them all the time," Ignatyev said.
Also in are youngsters Vitaly Abramov from league leaders Rotor Volgograd and Sergei Grishin of Dynamo Moscow.

The forward line retains a strong Latin flavour, however. Rotor's Denis Zubko is back in the squad, but also recalled are Santander's Vladimir Beschastnykh and Zaragoza's Vladislav Radimov. Spartak Moscow's Andrei Tikhonov has been out injured.
Out, too, is Alania Vladikavkaz forward Anatoly Kanishchev, who was suspended after failing to show up in Cyprus.

The Russians, who trounced Luxembourg 4-0 away last November despite playing most of the match with 10 men, are determined not to repeat the slip-up in Cyprus which has left them trailing Israel and Bulgaria at the half-way stage.
Russia host Israel in June. Most see the group being decided by two Russia-Bulgaria encounters scheduled after the summer.
Goalkeepers - Sergei Ovchinnikov (Lokomotiv Moscow), Stanislav Cherchesov (Tirol Innsbruck)
Defenders - Ramiz Mamedov (Spartak Moscow), Maxim Bokov (CSKA Moscow), Igor Chugaynov (Lokomotiv Moscow), Viktor Onopko (Oviedo), Yuri Kovtun (Dynamo Moscow), Dmitry Popov (Compostela).

Midfielders - Andrei Kanchelskis (Fiorentina), Sergei Grishin (Dynamo), Omari Tetradze (Roma), Igor Yanovsky (Alania Vladikavkaz), Valery Kechinov, Ilya Tsymbalar, Dmitry Alenichev (all Spartak), Vitaly Abramov (Rotor Volgograd), Alexander Gorshkov (Zhemchuzhina Sochi).
Forwards - Vladimir Kulik (CSKA), Denis Zubko (Rotor), Igor Simutenkov (Reggiana), Vladimir Beschastnykh (Racing Santander), Alexei Gerasimenko (Rostselmash Rostov), Vladislav Radimov (Zaragoza).
